html:
Guinea-Bissau is a small country on the West African coast, between Senegal and Guinea. On the map it covers the colony of Portuguese Guinea and the republic that won independence from it.

The land was once part of the Mali Empire and then the Mandinka kingdom of Kaabu. From the 1500s Portugal traded for slaves at coastal posts such as Cacheu and Bissau, but it controlled the interior only in the early 1900s.

In 1963 the party of Amílcar Cabral began a guerrilla war for this colony and for Cape Verde. Cabral was murdered in January 1973. His movement declared independence that September, and Portugal accepted it in 1974 after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon.

Since then the country has had a one-party state, a civil war in 1998 to 1999, and many coups, the latest in 2025. It has also become a transit point for cocaine smuggled to Europe.
sum: Guinea-Bissau is a small country on the West African coast, between Senegal and Guinea. On the map it covers the colony of Portuguese Guinea and the republic that won independence from it.
